record.paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
record.original_question: Let {alpha_k}_{k>=0} and {beta_k}_{k>=0} be classical multiplier sequences consisting of nonnegative real numbers, where a classical multiplier sequence is a real sequence whose diagonal operator T[x^k]=gamma_k x^k preserves real-rootedness of real polynomials. Characterize all functions Psi: R x R -> R such that, for every such pair {alpha_k} and {beta_k}, the pointwise sequence {Psi(alpha_k,beta_k)}_{k>=0} is again a classical multiplier sequence.

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Let {alpha_k}_0^infinity and {beta_k}_0^infinity be multiplier sequences of non-negative real numbers. Characterize all functions Psi : R x R -> R such that {Psi(alpha_k, beta_k)}_0^infinity is again a multiplier sequence.

Definition 5. A sequence of real numbers {gamma_k}_0^infinity is called a classical multiplier sequence if the associated linear operator T defined by T[x^k]=gamma_k x^k has the property that for every real polynomial p(x), Z_C(T[p(x)])=0 whenever Z_C(p(x))=0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is called a classical multiplier sequence if the linear operator $T$ defined on $\mathbb{R}[x]$ by $T[x^k]=\gamma_k x^k$ has the property that for every real polynomial $p(x)$ whose complex zeros are all real, the polynomial $T[p(x)]$ also has only real zeros (with the convention that the zero polynomial qualifies).

Characterize all functions $\Psi:\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ with the following property: whenever $\{\alpha_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ and $\{\beta_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ are classical multiplier sequences consisting of nonnegative real numbers, the pointwise sequence $\{\Psi(\alpha_k,\beta_k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is again a classical multiplier sequence.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on multiplier sequences and generalized Bessel functions. No published characterization of all such bivariate transformations $\Psi$ preserving classical multiplier sequences on nonnegative inputs was found; only partial results (e.g., for sums, products, and specific algebraic combinations) are known.
